findings.text: The first paragraph tells a newcomer what Athena is, who it is for, and why it matters, in plain words. The reader can answer all three in under a minute.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository. ... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The next step is concrete and complete: what you need first, how to clone, how to install, and a first command to try. A link near the top ("install Athena or read firstmate itself") jumps straight there.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" … "./setup.sh" … "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Someone visiting Athena's home URL meets a title about another project, firstmate. The page has to explain that it is a study before the reader knows why firstmate matters to them, which may make them think they landed on the wrong page.
findings.source: <title>Athena explains how firstmate handles work</title> and h1 of the same text

findings.text: The page promises Athena's main output: a commit traced to the request, models, cost and verdict. It never shows one. Almost the whole page demonstrates a side skill, reading another project, so the main value is stated but not shown.
findings.source: "records what each step cost" / "get back a commit they can trace to the request, the models, the cost and the verdict"

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed state machine of firstmate's internals: exit codes, pending-close records, places-held. It works as evidence of rigour, but a newcomer will likely skim or stop here. Nothing tells them they can skip it.
This header link speaks to an owner, not a visitor, and says nothing about whose proposals these are. A newcomer cannot tell whether it is meant for them.
findings.source: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: This uses internal terms ("job", "recorded boundary", "marked read") that are never explained to an outside reader. The "About this page" section's reference to a "folder under studies/" is the same: internal detail with no meaning to a visitor.
findings.source: Limits of this study, f1: "The job gave no recorded boundary for running firstmate, so no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: Defining terms before they are used, and again in a glossary, makes the firstmate jargon easier to follow for a reader who does go deeper.
